title: Ask a favour to make someone like you

lines.text: Want someone to like you more? Ask them for a favour.
Benjamin Franklin had a political rival who disliked him.
So Franklin asked to borrow a rare book from the man's library.
The rival lent it. Franklin returned it with a warm thank you note.
After that, the rival started speaking to him, and they became lifelong friends.
In 1969, psychologists Jecker and Landy put it to the test.
People asked directly by a researcher to return their winnings ended up liking him more than people who weren't asked.
Your brain sees itself helping, and decides, I must like this person.
So next time, don't do someone a favour. Let them do one for you.

sources.claim: Franklin borrowed a rare book from a rival legislator, who then became a lasting friend
Jecker and Landy (1969): students personally asked by the researcher to return winnings liked him most; asked via a secretary liked him least

publish.title: Ask for a Favour to Make Someone Like You 🤝
